theory.intro: The **population** is every individual or item being investigated. A **census** collects data from the whole population; a **sample** collects data from part of it. Name the population first — the same data can be a census of one and a sample of another.
facts: The **population** is every individual or item being investigated — not just the ones who ended up being surveyed.
A census can cover millions of people — a large population does **not** make a study a sample.
What matters is whether **everyone** in the population was included, not how many people there are.
A sample is used when the population is too large, or when a census would cost too much or take too long.
A sample is also needed when testing destroys the item, such as crash-testing a helmet or opening a jar to check its seal.
Because a census includes everyone its result is exact, while a sample only estimates the population's result.

foundation.question_text: Data is collected from **every** member of the population. What name is given to this type of data collection?
foundation.solution_text:
Data comes from the whole population.
**A census.**

foundation.question_text: Data is collected from only **part** of the population. What name is given to this type of data collection?
foundation.solution_text:
Data comes from part of the population.
**A sample.**

foundation.question_text: A school with $940$ students gives its lunch-quality survey to every student in the school, to find out what the school's students think. Is this a census or a sample?
foundation.solution_text:
The population is all $940$ students at the school.
Every one of them was surveyed.
**Census.**

foundation.question_text: One Year $8$ class of $28$ students is surveyed to find out what all $940$ students at the school think of the lunches. Is this a census or a sample?
foundation.solution_text:
The population is all $940$ students at the school.
Only $28$ of them were surveyed.
**Sample.**

foundation.question_text: Scientists tag and track $200$ of the $3500$ humpback whales in Australian waters to study their migration. Is this a census or a sample?
foundation.solution_text:
The population is all $3500$ whales.
Only $200$ of them were tracked.
**Sample.**

foundation.question_text: Every five years the Australian Government collects information from every resident of Australia. Is this a census or a sample?
foundation.solution_text:
The population is every resident of Australia.
Information is collected from all of them.
**Census.**

foundation.question_text: An automatic scale on a factory line weighs every jar of sauce produced during a shift. Is this a census or a sample of that shift's jars?
foundation.solution_text:
The population is every jar produced during the shift.
All of them are weighed.
**Census.**

foundation.question_text: A phone factory takes every tenth screen off the line and tests it for scratches. Is this a census or a sample?
foundation.solution_text:
The population is all the screens produced.
Only every tenth screen is tested.
**Sample.**

development.question_text: A ranger examines $60$ of the little penguins in a colony to check the health of the colony. State the population, and whether this is a census or a sample.
development.solution_text:
Population: **all the little penguins in the colony**.
Only $60$ of them were examined.
**Sample.**

development.question_text: A helmet factory crash-tests $20$ helmets taken from a batch of $5000$ before the batch is sold. State the population, and whether this is a census or a sample.
development.solution_text:
Population: **all $5000$ helmets in the batch**.
Only $20$ of them were tested.
**Sample.**

development.question_text: A carnival organiser wants to know which sports **Year $7$ students** want at the carnival, and asks all $120$ Year $7$ students at the school. State the population, and whether this is a census or a sample.
development.solution_text:
Population: **all $120$ Year $7$ students**.
Every one of them was asked.
**Census.**

development.question_text: In a school of $800$ students, the SRC asks all $150$ Year $9$ students about canteen prices and reports what **the whole school** thinks. State the population, and whether this is a census or a sample.
development.solution_text:
Population: **all $800$ students at the school**.
Only the $150$ Year $9$ students were asked.
**Sample.**

development.question_text: A sauce factory checks that jars are sealed correctly by opening a jar and testing its seal. Explain why the factory must use a sample rather than a census.
development.solution_text:
Testing a jar destroys it, because the jar has to be opened.
A census would mean opening every jar, leaving nothing to sell.
**A sample must be used.**

development.question_text: A teacher wants the average time her class of $25$ students spent on homework last night. Should she use a census or a sample? Justify your answer.
development.solution_text:
The population is only the $25$ students in the class.
Asking all $25$ is quick, and it gives the exact average instead of an estimate.
**A census.**

development.question_text: The national census is run only once every five years rather than every year. Give one reason why a government would not collect data from every resident more often.
development.solution_text:
Collecting and processing an answer from every single resident costs an enormous amount of money and takes a long time.
**Cost and time are why a census of a whole country is run only rarely.**

mastery.question_text: Marcus says the Australian Census cannot really be a census, because $26$ million people is far too many for anyone to collect data from everyone. Explain why Marcus is incorrect, and describe what would make the collection a sample instead.
mastery.solution_text:
Whether a collection is a census depends on **who is included**, not on how large the population is.
The Census collects data from every resident of Australia, so it covers the whole population.
It would only be a sample if data were collected from part of the population — for example, from $10\,000$ selected households.
**A large population does not turn a census into a sample.**

mastery.question_text: A match factory tests match quality by striking matches to see whether they light. Explain why a census is impossible here, and describe a sample the quality team could take instead.
mastery.solution_text:
Striking a match destroys it, because a used match cannot be sold.
A census would mean striking every match the factory makes, leaving none to sell, so a census is impossible.
Instead the team could strike a few matches from selected boxes, such as $5$ matches from every hundredth box.
**Only a sample can be used when testing destroys the item.**

mastery.question_text: A ranger counts every one of the $74$ koalas living inside a fenced sanctuary. The sanctuary manager wants to know how many koalas live in the sanctuary, while a state scientist wants to know how many koalas live in the whole state. Explain why the same count is a census for one of them and a sample for the other.
mastery.solution_text:
For the manager the population is the $74$ koalas in the sanctuary, and all $74$ of them were counted, so the count is a **census**.
For the scientist the population is every koala in the state, and the sanctuary koalas are only a small part of it, so the same count is a **sample**.
The label depends on the population being investigated, not on how the data was gathered.
